title: M08-Reflection Essay-Advanced Data Types
text:
Managing Data Complexity with R
In this module, we explored how to handle various data types efficiently using specialized R packages.
Three essential functions for data wrangling:

str_detect(): Identifying patterns in character strings for filtering.
ymd(): Converting inconsistent date text into standardized date objects.
fct_reorder(): Managing categorical data by reordering factor levels based on numeric values.

title: M08-Reflection Essay-Advanced Data Types
text:
Date-Time Handling Strategies
Handling date-time data is often one of the most complex tasks in data science.
Key Insights

Standardizing formats early prevents downstream errors.
Extracting components (year, month, day) allows for granular temporal analysis.
lubridate provides a grammatical approach to time-based transformations.

title: M12-Reflection Essay-Advanced R Programming
text:
Reducing Repetition with Functions
Efficiency in programming is driven by reducing redundant code.

Abstraction: Encapsulating logic into reusable functions.
Readability: Making workflows easier for others (and future self) to follow.
The Rule of Three: If you repeat a task three times, it’s time to write a function.

title: M12-Reflection Essay-Advanced R Programming
text:
Functional Programming with {purrr}
Replacing traditional loops with cleaner iteration using the map() family of functions.

library(purrr)
# Example: Computing means across multiple columns
cols <- c("mpg", "hp", "wt")
map_dbl(mtcars[cols], mean)

      mpg        hp        wt 
 20.09062 146.68750   3.21725
